excluded.hesychius-antioch: no life written: App names Holy Martyr Hesychius of Antioch on 03-02. OCA March 2 lists Hieromartyr Theodotus of Cyrenia, Arseny of Tver, 440 Martyrs of Lombardy, and Martyr Euthalia; Orthocal 3/2 lists the same. No Hesychius appears on either source for that date, so no life was written.
excluded.agabus-apostle: no life written: App names Holy Apostle Agabus on 03-15. OCA March 15 lists Martyr Agapius and Seven with Him and Martyr Alexander (270-275); Orthocal 3/15 lists the same two. Agabus is not named on either source for that date (and OCA's page has no mention of Agabus), so no life was written.
excluded.martyr-niketas-gothi: no life written: App names Holy Martyr Niketas of the Goths on 03-20. OCA March 20 lists Holy Fathers Slain at St Sabbas Monastery, Myron the New Martyr of Crete, Photine the Samaritan Woman and Cuthbert of Lindisfarne; Orthocal 3/20 lists the same. Niketas the Goth is not named for that date in either source (OCA's page does not mention him), so no life was written.
excluded.anastasia-rome-martyr: no life written: OCA April 20 lists Theodore Trichinas, Athanasios of Meteora, Apostle Zaccheus, and others; no Anastasia of Rome appears there, and Orthocal 4/20 names only Theodore Trichinas, Athanasios of Meteora and Zaccheus. OCA places 'Martyrs Basilissa and Anastasia of Rome, disciples of the Apostles' on April 15 (1st c., under Nero). Date mismatch or different identity; no life written.
excluded.theodotus-ancyra: no life written: App date is 05-16. OCA May 16 and Orthocal 5/16 do not name Theodotus; both list Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra (innkeeper, with the seven virgins, under Decius/Diocletian) on May 18. Date mismatch; no life written.
excluded.peter-caesarea-cappadocia: no life written: OCA May 18 names Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra and the Martyrs Peter, Dionysius, Andrew, Paul, Christina (Lampsacus, under Decius); Orthocal 5/18 similar. No 'Venerable Peter of Caesarea in Cappadocia' appears for May 18 (nor on May 16/17 OCA pages checked). Unidentified; no life written.
excluded.theodotus-ancyra-bishop: no life written: App entry is inconsistent: id 'theodotus-ancyra-bishop' but name/notes are 'Hieromartyr Marcellus, Bishop of Rome (+309)'. OCA (June 7) and Orthocal list Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Ancyra, and Hieromartyr Marcellinus, Pope of Rome (+304, under Diocletian), who is a different person from Pope Marcellus I (+309); Marcellus appears on that date only as Marcellinus's successor in a vision. No life written; the entry needs a decision between Theodotus of Ancyra or Marcellinus of Rome.
excluded.paul-peter-apostles-forefeast: no life written: App names a Forefeast of Sts Peter and Paul on 06-28. OCA all-lives for June 28 and Orthocal list only: Translation of Relics of Cyrus and John, Xenophon of Robeika, Sergius and Herman of Valaam, Paul of Corinth, Icon of the Three Hands, Hieromartyr Basil, Sergius of Paphlagonia (Orthocal adds Pappias, Sennuphius). Neither names a forefeast of Peter and Paul.
excluded.paisios-great: no life written: App names Paisios the Great on 07-09. OCA all-lives for July 9 lists Pancratius of Taormina, Cyril of Gortyna, Patermuthius, Coprius and Alexander, Theodore of Edessa, Dionysios the Rhetorician and Metrophanes, and two Theotokos icons; Orthocal lists Pancratius and Patermuthius. Neither mentions Paisios.
excluded.phocas-bishop-sinope: no life written: App names Hieromartyr Phocas of Sinope on 07-23. OCA all-lives for July 23 lists Trophimus and 14 others in Lycia, Hieromartyr Apollinaris of Ravenna, two Theotokos icons, and Anna of Leukadio (Orthocal adds Ezekiel and Anna mother of Samuel). No Phocas appears on that date.
excluded.cosmas-damian-arabia: no life written: Date mismatch. OCA and Orthocal for Oct 12 list Martyrs Probus, Tarachus and Andronicus, and Symeon the New Theologian (OCA also notes Cosmas the Hymnographer in Slavic usage). The Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Arabia (Cilicia) appear on OCA Oct 17, not Oct 12.
excluded.cornelius-centurion: no life written: Date mismatch. OCA and Orthocal for Oct 13 list Martyrs Carpus, Papylus, Agathodorus and Agathonica, and Martyr Zlata (Chryse) (plus Benjamin, Florentios in OCA). Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion is on OCA Sept 13.
excluded.miracle-chonae: no life written: Date mismatch. OCA and Orthocal for Nov 9 list Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius, Nektarios of Aegina, John the Dwarf, Matrona, Symeon Metaphrastes; no Chonae/Colossae miracle. OCA commemorates the Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Colossae on Sept 6 (OCA Sept 6 page).
excluded.erasmus-of-ohrid: no life written: App names Holy Martyrs Orestes and Erasmus of Ohrid on 11-10. OCA lives page for November 10 lists Apostles of the Seventy Erastus, Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Quartus and Tertius; Martyr Orestes the Physician of Cappadocia (Tyana, d. 304; OCA states he is not Orestes of Sebaste); Hieromartyr Milos of Persia; Theocteristus of Symbola; Constantine-Kakhi of Georgia; Great-martyr George of Georgia. No Erasmus and no Ohrid saint appears (the word Erasmus/Ohrid is absent from the page). Orthocal for 11-10 lists Apostles Erastus et al. and Arsenios of Cappadocia only. Entry looks like a conflation of Orestes of Tyana with an unattested Erasmus; no life written.
excluded.martyrs-persia-shapur: no life written: App names Holy Martyrs and Confessors of Persia on 11-15. OCA lives page for November 15 lists Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samonas and Habibus of Edessa (under Diocletian/Maximian and Licinius, not Persia); Martyrs Elpidius, Marcellus and Eustochius (under Julian); Martyr Demetrios of Thrace; and Paisios Velichkovsky. Orthocal for 11-15 lists the start of the Nativity Fast, Gurias, Shamuna and Habib of Edessa, and Paisius Velichkovsky. Neither source names a Persian martyrs group or Shapur on this date; no life written.
excluded.thyrsus-leucius-philemon: no life written: App names Holy Martyrs Thyrsus, Leucius, and Philemon (Caesarea in Phrygia) on 12-14. OCA lives page for December 14 lists Martyrs Thyrsos, Leukios and Kallinikos, who suffered under Decius at Caesarea in Bithynia, and, as a separate commemoration, Martyrs Philemon, Apollonios, Arrian and Theonas of Alexandria (c. 290-305). Orthocal likewise lists 'Thyrsus, Leucis, Callinicus' and 'Philemon, Apollonius, Arian and those with them'. No trio including both Leucius and Philemon exists in the calendar; the third name and the place (Bithynia, not Phrygia) differ. No life written.

flags.irene-great-martyr: Written 2026-10-01 for the corrected May 5 entry; details are from the saint's traditional life.
flags.theodotus-ancyra: OCA's heading says the martyrs suffered under Decius, while its narrative places Theodotus under Diocletian (c. 303); dating is therefore uncertain.
flags.theodotus-ancyra-bishop: The OCA title calls him 'Hieromartyr ... Bishop of Ancyra', but its text and Orthocal's story describe a lay Christian and never mention a bishopric; this is the same man commemorated May 18 (OCA notes this).
flags.agabus-apostle: Death and later ministry are only generally described; no specific place of death given.
flags.cosmas-damian-arabia: Century differs: OCA's app note says 3rd; Orthocal says 4th. OCA text names no century. Distinct from the pairs of Nov 1 and Jul 1.
flags.thyrsus-leucius-philemon: App id says 'Philemon' and app notes say Phrygia, but OCA names Callinicus as the third martyr and places Caesarea in Bithynia; Philemon is a separate Dec 14 martyr of Alexandria. Id/notes should be corrected.
flags.cornelius-centurion: OCA titles him Hieromartyr, but its narrative says he died in old age and does not describe martyrdom; app type 'saint' and name 'Martyr' differ.
flags.basil-great-circumcision: The calendar names both items on Jan 1; the app's rank note (rank 2, St Basil as Polyeleos saint) was not checked against a source. Orthocal lists the feast as 'Circumcision of Our Lord' with Basil among the saints.
flags.seraphim-sarov: Sources differ on birth year (OCA: 1754; Orthocal: 1759), so the birth year is omitted. Glorification year 1903 is inferred from OCA's mention of the manuscript found in 1903 'shortly before the glorification'; the app note gives 1903. OCA also lists the Forefeast of Theophany on this date.
flags.theodosius-cenobiarch: Death year differs: app note says 529; Orthocal heading gives 519; OCA gives only 'fifth-sixth centuries'. Age at death also differs (OCA 105; Great Horologion via Orthocal 103). Dates are left general.
flags.gregory-theologian: The app note mentions a translation of Gregory's relics on another date; OCA mentions the transfer of his relics to Constantinople in 950 within this life but names no separate commemoration on Jan 25, so it is not treated as a separate item.
flags.translation-chrysostom: App note says 438; OCA text gives 438 in the body but the Orthocal heading gives 437. Used 438.
flags.ephrem-syrian: App note gives death year 373; neither fetched source states it (OCA gives no death year), so no year is stated. OCA also names Isaac the Syrian on this date; the app entry names only Ephraim.
flags.three-hierarchs: App note says the feast was established by 'Patriarch John Mauropos'; OCA names 'John, Bishop of Euchaita' and Orthocal 'the monk John Mauropus' (a reign of Alexios I Komnenos). He was not a patriarch in either source, and the app note should be corrected.
flags.annunciation-theotokos: App note about feast-rank overrides when March 25 coincides with Holy Week or Pascha was not checked in fetched sources.
flags.george-great-martyr: OCA calls him a native of Cappadocia yet places the serpent story at his native city of Beirut; Wikipedia says Cappadocian Greek origin. Life says 'said to be of Cappadocian origin'. OCA does not name the place of execution.
flags.mark-evangelist: Death year differs: OCA says 63; app notes and Wikipedia say c. 68. Life states both.
flags.constantine-helen-equal-apostles: Helen's death: OCA gives 327; app notes and Wikipedia give c. 330. Life says 'around 327'; consider 'c. 327-330'.
flags.third-finding-head-john-baptist: Only OCA gives the account; Orthocal confirms the date and name. No Wikipedia article found for this specific finding.
flags.dormition-theotokos: Details are from tradition (OCA draws on Nikephoros Callistus and others); Scripture is silent.
flags.beheading-john-baptist: OCA dates the martyrdom to 32; scholars give varying dates, so period is approximate. Place of execution not stated by OCA; life omits it.
flags.nativity-theotokos: OCA places the birth in Nazareth; other traditions differ (not fetched). Life follows OCA.
flags.exaltation-holy-cross: OCA and Wikipedia agree on 335; Heraclius's return is dated 628 by Wikipedia (OCA gives no year). Strict-fast-day detail in app notes not in fetched sources, so omitted from life.
flags.john-theologian-repose: Scholars debate whether the apostle authored all the Johannine writings; life follows Church tradition as stated by OCA.
flags.protection-theotokos: OCA notes historical uncertainty: Andrew's lifetime and the date of the vision are unclear, and Nestor's chronicle links the deliverance to a Rus' attack of 860-867 without mentioning Andrew. Life reflects this.
flags.synaxis-bodiless-hosts: Orthocal also lists the Synaxis of the Holy Unmercenaries on this date; it is not part of the app entry and is not covered. The date of the Laodicea council is given loosely by OCA.
flags.john-chrysostom: The app note mentions St Arcadius of Cyprus on Nov 13; neither the OCA page nor Orthocal for 2026 lists him on this date, so he is not covered. OCA says John's death on 14 September is commemorated on 13 November because of the Elevation of the Cross.
flags.apostle-philip: Orthocal's saints list for Nov 14 also names Gregory Palamas, Justinian and Theodora, and Constantine of Hydra; these are not part of the app entry.
flags.apostle-andrew-first-called: OCA's page also names Venerable Sebastian Dabovich and Orthocal names Frumentius of Ethiopia on this date; these are not part of the app entry.
flags.sabas-sanctified: OCA gives death 532, Orthocal 533. Orthocal also lists Cosmas the Protos of Athos; not part of the app entry.
flags.nicholas-myra: Orthocal also lists New Martyr Nicolas Karamos and Maximus of Kiev; not part of the app entry. Death year (345 in Orthocal) is not stated by OCA and is omitted.
flags.spyridon-trimythous: App note gives death as +348; neither OCA nor Orthocal states a death year, so it is omitted. OCA spells the see Tremithus and also lists Mardarije of Libertyville (not in the app entry).
flags.forefeast-nativity-eve: Orthocal lists the Eve of Nativity and Martyr Eugenia; Eugenia is not part of the app entry. The OCA text describes services only, with no narrative; the app's rank-1 treatment is the app's own choice.
flags.synaxis-theotokos-nativity: Orthocal also lists the Flight into Egypt, Euthymius of Sardis and Constantine of Synnada; these are not part of the app entry.
flags.protomartyr-stephen: In 2026 Dec 27 is a Sunday; OCA's page leads with David, Joseph and James of the Sunday after Nativity, with Stephen second. Orthocal lists Stephen as the feast.
flags.gregory-nyssa: Calendar also commemorates Dometian, Bishop of Melitene (6th c.) on Jan 10; the life is written for Gregory, the app's primary identity. Sources differ on birth year (331 in Orthocal; roughly 335 elsewhere), so no birth year is given.
flags.veneration-chains-peter: Sources agree on Acts 12 and on veneration of the chains; the later history of the relics (Constantinople, Rome) is tradition and varies by account.
flags.martyr-ignatius-god-bearer-translation: Year and details of the translation (108) come from tradition; sources agree on the return of the relics to Antioch but are brief.
flags.theodore-stratelates: Distinct from Theodore the Recruit (Feb 17); some traditions confuse the two.
flags.haralambos-martyr: Sources differ on his age at death (103 or 113) and on the location of Magnesia; age omitted.
flags.onesimus-apostle: New Testament gives only the Philemon story; later career and martyrdom are tradition.
flags.theodore-tyron: Date of death varies (303 to 306); the dragon story is a later legend. Distinct from Theodore Stratelates (Feb 8).
flags.finding-relics-innocent-irkutsk: DATE: Orthocal and OCA list Uncovering of relics of martyrs at the Gate of Eugenius on Feb 22 (Gregorian) and not Innocent. In the Russian (Julian) calendar the uncovering of Innocent's relics falls on Feb 9 O.S., which is Feb 22 N.S., so this is a Slavic-calendar entry. 1764 = discovery of incorrupt body; 1805 = formal uncovering/glorification (app says 'finding 1764').
flags.polycarp-smyrna: Date of martyrdom disputed (c. 155 or 167); stated approximately.
flags.forty-martyrs-sebaste: Sources differ slightly on details such as the guard's replacement and the fate of the relics.
flags.john-climacus: Orthocal says he entered at sixteen; OCA says little is known of his origins. Dates are approximate.
flags.mary-egypt: Orthocal notes the date of her repose is very unclear (378, 437 or 522 in different accounts); no year given.
flags.james-zebedee: Identity corrected in app: April 30 is James son of Zebedee (not James the Brother of the Lord, who is Oct 23). Orthocal's title reads 'brother of St John the Theologian'. Spain tradition is not historically established.
flags.athanasius-alexandria: May 2 is a secondary commemoration (translation of relics); main feast is Jan 18 with Cyril of Alexandria. Orthocal's May 2 entry points to Jan 18 for the life.
flags.simon-zealot-apostle: Accounts of his later mission and martyrdom vary; Cana bridegroom identification is tradition only.
flags.nina-georgia: IDENTITY/DATE: app id and name lead with the Fathers of the First Council of Nicaea, but the calendar for Jan 14 (OCA, Orthocal) gives Nina of Georgia (and the Fathers slain at Sinai and Raithu, and Sava of Serbia); the Nicaea fathers are commemorated on a Sunday in the Paschal season, not Jan 14. Life written for Nina.
flags.agape-irene-chionia: IDENTITY: app names Great Martyr Irene (+303, Diocletian). On Apr 16 the calendar (OCA, Orthocal) commemorates the Virgin Martyrs Agape, Irene and Chionia; the Great Martyr Irene is commemorated on May 5. Life written for the three sisters. Some Greek accounts place them at Thessalonica; sources differ on place.
flags.jude-apostle-brother-lord: Orthodox calendar treats Jude, Brother of the Lord (June 19) as distinct from Thaddaeus of the Twelve (June 21); the app note identifies him with Thaddaeus. Life written for the calendar identity. Wikipedia notes the identification is debated.
flags.euphemia-great-martyr: July 11 is the commemoration of the Chalcedon miracle in Slavic usage; her martyrdom is Sept 16 (see separate entry). Wikipedia dates her death 303; app note says 304.
flags.vladimir-equal-apostles: Orthocal gives death year 1051 in its title; the standard date is 1015.
flags.dormition-anna-mother-theotokos: Details of Anna's life rest on non-canonical tradition.
flags.matthias-apostle-august: Sources differ on where Matthias later preached.
flags.tikhon-zadonsk: DATE NOTE: OCA lists Tikhon on Aug 13, while Orthocal's Aug 26 lists Martyrs Adrian and Natalia. Aug 26 is the civil-calendar equivalent of Aug 13 Old Style (his repose, 1783), so the date is correct only for Julian-calendar Slavic usage. Check which calendar the app uses.
flags.deposition-belt-theotokos: Sources differ on what the feast commemorates; the app's 395 date is approximate.
flags.euphemia-all-praised-september: Duplicate saint of the July 11 entry; this one is the martyrdom feast. Life text differs deliberately.
flags.eustathios-thespesia-companions: Hadrian's reign is 117-138; the app's +118 is approximate. The saints are Eustathios, Theopiste and their sons.
flags.thekla-equal-apostles: Her story comes from an apocryphal text.
flags.thomas-maleon: Rewritten 2026-10-01 from the OCA lives page after the first draft wrongly placed Mount Maleon near Mount Athos.
flags.paraskeva-serbia: Calendar names her 'Parasceva of Serbia'; she is the same as Paraskeva the New / of the Balkans, born in Thrace (Epivates), venerated in Serbia because her relics rested in Belgrade. Distinct from Paraskeva of Rome (July 26) and Paraskeva Friday (Oct 28). Dates of life vary by source.
flags.james-brother-lord: Identity matches the calendar (James the Brother of the Lord, Oct 23; distinct from James son of Zebedee, Apr 30). No mismatch; noted because of the earlier mislabelling.
flags.cosmas-damian-asia: App lists type 'martyr'; calendar tradition for Nov 1 says these Asian unmercenaries reposed in peace rather than suffering martyrdom (the martyr pairs are Roman, July 1, and Arabian, Oct 17). Dates are traditional and uncertain.
flags.john-the-merciful: Date of death differs by source (616 vs 619).
flags.great-martyr-catherine: Historicity of details is debated; the emperor named differs by source (Maximian/Maxentius).
flags.clement-rome: Nov 25 also has the Leavetaking of the Entrance (separate entry).
flags.barbara-great-martyr: Place and date vary between sources; Orthocal lists the year as 290, the app notes say 306.
flags.john-damascene: Orthocal gives death year 760; most sources give c. 749.
flags.ignatius-god-bearer: Dec 20 also has the Forefeast of the Nativity.
flags.great-martyr-anastasia: Place of martyrdom varies by source (Sirmium or an island near Rome). The epithet and details are traditional.
flags.twenty-thousand-martyrs-nicomedia: Year differs (302 vs 303); the number and details come from tradition rather than contemporary records.
flags.gordius-caesarea: Sources differ on the year of martyrdom: OCA says 320, Orthocal says 314 (reign of Licinius); the life gives no year.
flags.forefeast-theophany: OCA and Orthocal name the martyrs as Theopemptus and Theonas (Orthocal dates them ca. 290; OCA says 303). Orthocal also lists Apollinaria and Syncletica on this date. Life covers the forefeast and Theopemptus/Theonas only.
flags.domnica-constantinople: Sources differ on her origin: OCA says she came from Carthage; Orthocal says she was born in Rome (and sailed via Alexandria). Orthocal dates her ca. 474; app notes say c.473. Life omits origin.
flags.leavetaking-theophany: Date confirmed: OCA and Orthocal both place the Leavetaking of Theophany on January 14. Entry is a feast, not a person.
flags.maximus-confessor: Birthplace: OCA says Constantinople; Orthocal notes a recently discovered account suggesting Palestine. Life omits birthplace.
flags.xenophon-family: Period: OCA says fifth century (heading V-VI); Orthocal places Xenophon in the reign of Justinian (6th c.). Life says only that they lived in Constantinople.
flags.tryphon-martyr: Place: OCA heading reads 'of Lampsacus near Apamea in Syria'; the text itself places his martyrdom at Nicaea. App name says Apamea.
flags.agatha-catania: Birthplace: OCA says Palermo; Orthocal says Catania or Palermo. OCA and Orthocal title her 'of Palermo'; app says 'of Catania' (martyrdom place). Same saint.
flags.leavetaking-presentation: Date confirmed: OCA and Orthocal list the Leavetaking of the Meeting on February 9. Entry is a feast, not a person.
flags.martinian-caesarea: Location of his first desert: OCA says near Caesarea in Palestine; Orthocal says a mountain in Cappadocia. Life follows OCA and the app name.
flags.archippus-apostle: OCA: Archippus slashed with knives under Nero; Philemon and Apphia stoned, fellow-workers. Orthocal: Archippus is Philemon's son and was stoned under governor Androcles. Life notes the difference without choosing.
flags.leo-catania: Minor difference: Orthocal says Leo was first bishop of Ravenna; OCA says priest at Ravenna. Life says only that he was born there.
flags.procopius-decapolites: OCA spells the name Prokopios; Orthocal gives 'Procopius of Decapolis (9th c.)', OCA gives 8th century and c.750.
flags.martyr-eudokia: Sources differ on the emperor (Trajan or Hadrian) and details of her later life; the app's '+2nd c.' is consistent. OCA and Orthocal spell the name Eudokia/Eudoxia.
flags.gerasimus-jordan: OCA and Orthocal give slightly different details (Orthocal gives repose in 475 and attendance at Chalcedon); main facts agree.
flags.mark-the-ascetic: Sources differ: OCA says he was born in Athens; Orthocal calls him a disciple of John Chrysostom. The life omits both. OCA has two figures on March 5 named Mark; this is the Ascetic of Egypt.
flags.forty-two-martyrs-ammoria: Minor: OCA places Amorion in 'Galicia' and Phrygia; Orthocal (Phrygia, 838, beheaded 845) is used. Euphrates detail from OCA only.
flags.hieromartyrs-cherson: Sources differ on how Aetherius died (OCA: died of illness on a journey; Orthocal notes the Prologue says in peace, the Horologion says drowned); the life says only that he governed in peace.
flags.martyr-codratus-corinth: App says +258 under Valerian; OCA and Orthocal place the Corinth martyrdom under Decius (249-251). OCA's entry is titled 'Quadratus', the same name as Codratus. The life omits the date and emperor. OCA also has a separate Quadratus of Nicomedia on this date.
flags.theophanes-confessor: Sources differ on details: OCA says he died in prison after 23 days; Orthocal says exile on Samothrace after two years of imprisonment. The life says only imprisoned and died.
flags.nikephoros-patriarch-constantinople: Date of death differs slightly between sources (OCA 828, Orthocal about 827); the app entry is the translation of relics, not his main feast.
flags.sabin-egypt: Date (287) given by OCA; Orthocal gives no date. OCA also briefly lists Sabinus on March 13.
flags.alexios-man-of-god: Sources differ on the years spent at Edessa (OCA 17, Orthocal 18); the life uses OCA and calls the account traditional.
flags.james-confessor: OCA lists James of Catania; Orthocal on this date lists only a James, Bishop of the Studion (different wording, location unknown). The identification of the Studite James with Catania rests on OCA alone.
flags.basil-ancyra-presbyter: Sources differ on the manner of death (OCA: red-hot rods, Orthocal: iron spits); the life says only that he died from the tortures. Orthocal calls him a bishop; OCA a presbyter.
flags.nikon-and-companions: Number of companions differs: OCA says 199 monks beheaded (190 monks entrusted to Nikon plus former soldiers), Orthocal says 190 perished. OCA gives no emperor; Orthocal places it under Decius, consistent with the app's +251.
flags.hilarion-new-pelekete: Sources differ: OCA places his death in 754 (under Constantine V, by Lakhanodrakon's raid); Orthocal says he was exiled with forty monks under Leo the Isaurian and died near Ephesus. The life gives no emperor. The app calls him a monastic; OCA says he died for the icons.
flags.mark-bishop-arethusa: OCA and Orthocal both say Mark was released after torture, not killed; he is a hieromartyr by title. The app says martyrs '+362' (under Julian); sources place the persecution then but do not report Mark's death.
flags.titus-wonder-worker: Orthocal says he became abbot of a monastery; OCA says hieromonk. The life follows OCA.
flags.nicetas-medikion: Details of imprisonment differ somewhat between OCA and Orthocal; the life follows OCA on the main facts.
flags.claudius-diodorus-victor-papias: OCA April 5 only lists 'Martyr Claudius and those with him' (Claudius, Diodoros, Victor, Victorinus, Pappios, Serapion, Nikephoros) with a note that they are probably the group of January 31; no separate life. Orthocal 4/5 does not list them. The life draws on OCA January 31 (https://www.oca.org/saints/all-lives/2026/01/31).
flags.eutychios-patriarch-constantinople: Sources differ on his role at the council (OCA: convened it; Orthocal: representative of the Metropolitan of Amasea). The life says only that he took part.
flags.antipas-pergamon: App notes give ca. 92 AD; OCA dates his death to the reign of Nero (ca. 68). Sources differ, so no precise date is given in the life.
flags.basil-bishop-parium: App lists him as 'Hieromartyr' with '+3rd c.'; OCA calls him Basil the Confessor, Bishop of Parium, 8th century, an iconoclast-era confessor who died in peace, not a martyr. Orthocal also lists 'St Basil the Confessor'. Type/title/century in app likely need correcting.
flags.symeon-bishop-persia: App notes give +341 and place the saint at Seleucia-Ctesiphon; OCA gives 344 and does not name the see. Sources differ on the year; the life gives OCA's date.
flags.john-disciple-gregory-theologian: App name says disciple of 'St. Gregory the Theologian'; OCA and Orthocal name him disciple of Gregory of Decapolis (Nov 20). Same commemoration (April 18), but the name in the app appears wrong.
flags.basil-bishop-amasea: OCA gives the account in detail; Wikipedia notes the Acts of his martyrdom are considered legendary. Life keeps to the core facts (bishop under Licinius, martyred c. 322).
flags.memnou-memnon-wonder-worker: App calls him 'Holy Martyr Memnon the Wonder-Worker (+3rd c.)'; OCA lists 'Venerable Memnon the Wonderworker', an Egyptian desert abbot, with no martyrdom and no century given. Orthocal for April 29 does not list him. Type and period in app need checking.
flags.germanus-constantinople: Orthocal's May 12 list names only Epiphanius; OCA's May 12 page includes Germanus the Patriarch, so the commemoration is confirmed there.
flags.glyceria-martyr: App notes say +177 under Marcus Aurelius; OCA says second century under Antoninus (138-161). Sources differ; life omits the emperor's name and exact date.
flags.simeon-stylites-junior: Sources differ on dates (OCA: born 521, died 596; Orthocal: born 522; app notes say +592). Life gives only 'late sixth century'.
flags.carpos-alphaeus-apostles: Same commemoration lists Carpos with Alphaeus; app id 'carpos-alphaeus-apostles' but name covers Carpos only. Sources differ on his see (Verria/Berea vs Thrace/Varna).
flags.theodosia-caesarea-cappadocia: App says 'Theodosia of Caesarea in Cappadocia'. OCA and Orthocal for May 29 name Virgin Martyr Theodosia of Tyre, martyred at Caesarea in PALESTINE under Maximian/Diocletian era (307/308); no Cappadocian Theodosia is listed. Life written for Theodosia of Tyre; app name/place should be corrected. (OCA also lists a separate Theodosia the Nun of Constantinople, 730, same date.)
flags.nicephorus-patriarch-cp: App title says 'Translation of the Relics'. OCA and Orthocal for June 2 list St Nikephoros the Confessor (his main commemoration), with the 846 return of relics mentioned in the same entry; life covers both.
flags.lucian-antioch-martyr: App id says 'lucian-antioch-martyr' but name/notes are Lucillian of Byzantium (correct for June 3); Hieromartyr Lucian of Beauvais is a separate saint listed the same day.
flags.bessarion-egypt: OCA's life names him a disciple of Isidore of Pelusium; app notes say disciple of Anthony and Moses the Ethiopian and dated c.466. Omitted as sources are unclear.
flags.alexander-antonina-martyrs: App says martyrs 'of Caesarea in Cappadocia'. OCA says Antonina was from Krodamos (Asia Minor) and heads the entry 'at Constantinople'; Orthocal places the trial in Alexandria. Sources differ on location; life names no specific city of martyrdom.
flags.leontius-martyr: App notes say Leontius '+2nd c.'; OCA and Orthocal place the martyrdom under Vespasian (1st century) and commemorate him with Hypatius and Theodulus.
flags.methodius-bishop-patara: Sources differ on his see (OCA: Patara; Orthocal: Patara or Olympus, then Tyre; martyred at Chalkis).
flags.febronia-nisibis: OCA says she was raised at Sivapolis in Assyria; Orthocal says Mesopotamia and martyred at Nisibis. Place given as Nisibis per the app's title.
flags.cosmas-damian-rome: Sources differ on the emperor (OCA names Carinus, Orthocal's Prologue note names Galerius); life omits his name.
flags.hyacinth-caesarea: Sources differ on length of his imprisonment (OCA: 38 days; Orthocal: eight days); life omits the figure.
flags.proclus-hilary-martyrs: Methods of execution differ between sources (OCA: arrows for Proclus; Orthocal: crucified); life follows OCA.
flags.macrina-sister-basil: Sources differ on death year (OCA: 380; Orthocal: 379); life gives no year.
flags.joseph-of-arimathea-nicodemus: OCA and Orthocal name only Righteous Joseph of Arimathea on 07-31 (with Eudocimus of Cappadocia); Nicodemus is not separately listed that day, and OCA marks the finding of his relics on 08-02. Life treats Joseph as the commemorated saint and mentions Nicodemus as in OCA's account.
flags.translation-stephen-protomartyr: App note gives 415; OCA says relics were found in 415 and moved to Constantinople about 428 (Orthocal says c. 427 for the discovery). Life follows OCA.
flags.dometius-persia: Orthocal notes the Great Horologion says he and his disciples were stoned; OCA and the Prologue say walled up. Life follows OCA.
flags.maximus-confessor-repose: App name/id say repose; OCA lists this day under 'Translation of the relics of St Maximus the Confessor', noting his main commemoration is January 21 (Orthocal lists Maximos on 08-13 with the same note). Life mentions both.
flags.thaddaeus-apostle: Sources differ on place and manner of death (peaceful repose at Beirut or Edessa vs. martyrdom per Orthocal and an Armenian tradition).
flags.eutyches-hieromartyr: Sources differ on his death: OCA full life and the Prologue say beheaded in his home city; the Great Horologion says he reposed in old age.
flags.alexander-john-paul-cp-patriarchs: Identity of Patriarch John differs: OCA notes John the Faster (+595) by one account, John Scholasticus (+577) by another.
flags.indiction-new-year: Sources differ on Symeon's birthplace (OCA full life: Sisan in Cappadocia; Orthocal: Syria); omitted.
flags.babylas-bishop-antioch: Sources differ on the emperor: OCA full life names Decius, while the short Orthocal life names Numerian; Decius used.
flags.autonomus-bishop-martyr: App notes place him in Paphlagonia; OCA says bishop in Italy martyred in Bithynia (near Soreus).
flags.sophia-vera-nadezda-lyubov: App name reads 'Sophia (Faith)'; OCA lists Sophia and her daughters Faith, Hope and Love.
flags.phocas-gardener-sinope: OCA's 09-22 list names 'Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope' (Orthocal likewise, under Trajan); OCA's full-life page also has 'Martyr Phokas the Gardener of Sinope' (not a hieromartyr). Date for Phocas the Gardener not given in text read, so period is uncertain.
flags.cyprian-ustyna-martyrs: OCA lists Hieromartyr Cyprian with Martyrs Justina and Theoctistus; app name omits Theoctistus. Wikipedia notes Catholic sources say no bishop of Antioch was named Cyprian and that the legend is of uncertain historicity; life framed as 'tradition holds'.
flags.hierotheos-bishop-athens: OCA calls him Hieromartyr; app type is 'hierarch'. OCA gives no details of his martyrdom.
flags.sergios-bacchus: Emperor named differs: OCA says Maximian, Wikipedia (hagiography) says Galerius; life omits the name.
flags.pelagia-penitent: Wikipedia notes scholarly debate over the origins and historicity of her story and gives 4th or 5th century.
flags.eulampios-eulampia: Emperor named differs: OCA says Maximian, Wikipedia says Maximinus; life omits the name.
flags.philip-apostle-october: OCA title: 'Apostle Philip of the Seventy' (one of the 7 Deacons); matches the app's identity.
flags.euthymios-thessalonica: App notes give death as 889; OCA and Wikipedia both give 898.
flags.hosea-prophet: Century differs: OCA says ninth century BC; app notes (and Wikipedia) say 8th century BC.
flags.artemios-antioch-martyr: Death year: Wikipedia gives 362; app notes say 363; OCA gives no year (Julian reigned 361-363).
flags.arethas-martyrs-nagran: OCA title is 'Martyr Arethas and Companions'; app calls him Great Martyr.
flags.martyrs-notarios: Death date: OCA says ca. 335; app notes say 351. Life gives only 'mid-fourth century'.
flags.nestor-martyr-thessalonica: OCA gives no year; app notes' '+306' not verified.
flags.terence-neonilla-family: OCA gives no date; app notes' '3rd c.' not verified.
flags.stephen-sabaite-hymnographer: OCA Oct 28 names 'Stephen the Hymnographer of Saint Savva Monastery' and does not give dates or the family link; Wikipedia gives 725-796 or 807 (app notes say +794). OCA says he may not be the Stephen of July 13.
flags.zenobius-zenobia: Year differs: OCA says 285; Wikipedia says c. 290.
flags.acepsimas-bishop-persia: OCA title lists only Acepsimus, Joseph and Aeithalas as companions; OCA gives no century (Sapor II context).
flags.galacteon-episteme: App notes say husband and wife; OCA title says wife but the narrative says betrothed who became monastics.
flags.thirty-three-martyrs-melitene: OCA titles the commemoration 'St Hieron and the Holy 33 Martyrs of Melitene'.
flags.plato-roman: App id is 'plato-roman' and notes give '+286'; OCA names Martyr Platon of Ancyra (listed with Romanus the Deacon) and gives no year or emperor for him. No death date included in life.
flags.stephen-younger: App lists type 'hierarch' with a hierarch troparion; OCA and Wikipedia describe him as a monk, martyr and confessor (not a bishop). OCA calls him 'Stephen the New'. Death year 764 is from Wikipedia; OCA text gives birth (715) but no death year in the portion read.
flags.patapius-thebes: OCA gives no century for Patapios; period is the app's estimate.
flags.boniface-tarsus: App notes give '+290'; OCA gives no year and Wikipedia gives 307, so no date stated.
flags.melania-roman: OCA names her husband Apinianus; Wikipedia gives Pinianus (same person).
